articles.title: AI, drones reshaping warfare, says Rajnath at Tarang Shakti finale
articles.summary: Rajnath Singh says AI, drones and electronic warfare are reshaping combat; at Tarang Shakti-2026 finale he urged stronger indigenous defence manufacturing.
articles.body: Jodhpur: Defence minister Rajnath Singh Saturday said future military strength would depend on a country’s ability to detect threats, assess situations and respond swiftly, as artificial intelligence (AI), drones and electronic warfare transform modern combat.Addressing the closing ceremony of the multinational air exercise Tarang Shakti-2026 at Jodhpur Air Force Station, Singh stressed the need to strengthen indigenous defence manufacturing and advanced military technologies to meet emerging security challenges.He said no country could sustain a prolonged conflict under uncertain circumstances without the capacity to manufacture its own weapons and develop critical technologies.Singh said India’s armed forces were undergoing structural, technological and strategic transformation. Unmanned systems and drones had changed the pace and scale of military operations, while AI was reshaping battlefield decision-making.Information, precision, speed and coordination between military systems would determine outcomes in future conflicts, he said, adding that electronic warfare required effective control over the electromagnetic spectrum.“Modern warfare was no longer confined to land, sea and air, with space, cyberspace, the electromagnetic spectrum and the information domain emerging as increasingly important operational areas,” he said.Highlighting indigenous capabilities, Singh cited the Tejas fighter aircraft and Akash missile defence system as examples of India’s technological progress. He expressed confidence that the country would make significant progress in developing fifth-generation fighter aircraft.The minister also called for deeper defence partnerships with friendly nations through joint research, development, training and co-production, rather than limiting cooperation to purchasing aircraft and weapons.Singh said the exercise, attended by observers from 32 countries, would strengthen mutual trust and facilitate the exchange of operational experience.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Jaipur | Silver Rate in Jaipur | Bank Holidays in Jaipur | Public Holidays in Jaipur | Jaipur AQI | Weather in Jaipur | Petrol Price in Jaipur | Diesel Price in Jaipur | CNG Price in Jaipur | LPG Price in JaipurStay updated with the latest Jaipur news. articles.title: 'No illegal detention, restore internet, metro services': Supreme Court after Delhi protest crackdown - top quotes
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that metro and railway
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that metro and railway services function normally. The court's directive came a day after Centre's crackdown on CJP's proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.The court issued notice to the Centre on a plea seeking contempt proceedings against authorities for allegedly violating its earlier directions on transport restrictions during the protest.“In view of the urgent applications alleging violation of our earlier order dt. October 9, 2026, and also alleging illegal detention of large number of individuals at Delhi on October 10, 2026 this court had assembled for an urgent hearing,” a bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said during a special sitting.“Senior counsels submitted there was a flagrant violation of the directions -- metro railway was not functioning, New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations remained closed, no traffic advisories were issued and a large number of persons were subjected to undue harassment and illegal detention even beyond the area which was covered by the prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023,” the bench said.The Supreme Court asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure that the Delhi Metro operated according to its normal schedule and that internet services were not disrupted, subject to law and order conditions. It also directed that lawyers, journalists and others should not be impeded from discharging their professional duties.Mehta, appearing for the Centre, defended the authorities’ action and submitted that entry and exit had been restricted at only 45 of the 303 stations across the Delhi Metro network on October 10.The court was also hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy concerning the detention of political leaders. It said it would grant a hearing to all lawyers involved in the matter.What the Supreme Court saidNo illegal detention: Authorities must ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained.Normal metro operations: The Centre was asked to ensure that Delhi Metro services function according to their normal schedule.Internet services: There should be no disruption to internet services, subject to law and order conditions.Professional duties: Lawyers, journalists and others must not be impeded from discharging their professional duties.Contempt proceedings: The court issued notice to the Centre on a plea alleging violation of its earlier directions.What is contempt plea aboutThe contempt petition, filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, names Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation chairperson D Thara as respondents.The plea refers to the Supreme Court’s October 9 order, passed while hearing a separate petition challenging the closure of 57 metro stations and the cancellation of trains to Delhi in view of the proposed protest. The latest applications alleged that the restrictions and detentions on October 10 violated the court’s directions.The court’s intervention followed the CJP’s call for a mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar, alongside student organisations, demanding action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.The government thwarted the planned demonstration through an extensive security crackdown across the national capital. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A day after police cracked down on the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) supremo Arvind Kejriwal
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A day after police cracked down on the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) supremo Arvind Kejriwal turned his fire on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, invoking Hitler to attack the Centre’s handling of the demonstration and warning that the demand for resignation could extend beyond CEC Gyanesh Kumar.In a video shared on X, Kejriwal accused the authorities of mistreating protesters, including young women, lawyers and journalists, during Saturday’s crackdown.Also read: Turn any spot into your own Jantar Mantar, says Arvind Kejriwal“The way Modi ji unleashed a reign of terror yesterday, he crossed all limits and left even Hitler behind. Videos of his atrocities are circulating everywhere. Young girls are being subjected to atrocities and mistreated. Lawyers were not spared, journalists were not spared — no one was spared. It should not come to a point where, along with Gyanesh Kumar, Modi ji himself is forced to resign this time,” Kejriwal said in a video message.The CJP had called for a mass demonstration at Jantar Mantar, demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over SIR. However, an extensive security crackdown significantly curtailed the planned protest, with police detaining party leaders and supporters across the national capital.CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were among those detained after arriving at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport. Police also detained several opposition leaders, including Kejriwal, West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, along with YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.READ ALSO: ‘Going home to be with family as my grandmother has passed away’: Abhijeet DipkeThe crackdown resulted in more than 7,000 detentions, triggering allegations of excessive restrictions on peaceful assembly and the treatment of protesters.The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Centre on a contempt plea alleging violation of its earlier directions and called for measures to prevent illegal detention of peaceful protesters and ensure normal transport services.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: PM Modi inaugurates Rs 4,900 crore Chennai Metro Phase II stretch, rides train with CM Vijay
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around Rs 4,900 crore.He also took a ride on the newly inaugurated stretch with Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay.PM Modi and Vijay jointly flagged off the new Metro services in the presence of Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar. The Prime Minister also purchased a ticket and briefly interacted with an employee at the ticket counter.The newly inaugurated stretch is part of Corridor 4 of Phase II and covers around 15 km, with 11 elevated Metro stations. The corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure and advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations.The new stretch is expected to reduce daily commuting time and improve connectivity between Chennai’s western suburbs and the city centre.Chennai Metro services: Timings and stationsAccording to Chennai Metro Rail, regular passenger services on the new stretch will begin at 4 pm on Sunday and operate in both directions until 9 pm. From October 12, services will run daily from 7 am to 9 pm.The last train will depart at 9 pm from both terminals: Poonamallee Bypass Metro and Vadapalani Metro on Corridor 4.The 11 stations on the new stretch are Poonamallee Bypass, Poonamallee Bus Stand, Poonamallee Government Hospital, Karayanchavadi, Kumananchavadi, Kattupakkam, Iyappanthangal, Thelliyaragaram, Porur Bypass, Porur Junction and Vadapalani.PM Modi offers prayersEarlier, Modi offered prayers at the Sri Jalakanteswara Swamy Temple in Tamil Nadu. He later visited the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras.The Prime Minister is also scheduled to dedicate the centre to the nation. The facility is part of a scientific initiative to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, covering different stages of life, from the foetal stage to old age.PM Modi will also release C-STROKE, a human ischaemic stroke atlas featuring more than 1,000 annotated microscopic sections from a stroke-affected brain. The atlas is expected to help researchers identify potential new targets for treatment.Later in the day, the Prime Minister is scheduled to attend the golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School.Highway, port and railway projects on agendaDuring his visit, Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for National Highway projects worth around Rs 3,700 crore in Tamil Nadu.The key projects include the 36-km, four-laned Vadugapatti-Therkuvenganallur section of NH-744A, the 30-km, four-laned Madurai Ring Road section of NH-744A, and the four-lane Thiruvarur Bypass on the Nagapattinam-Thanjavur section of NH-83.He will also inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal.Several port-related projects at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V O Chidambaranar Port are also on the agenda. These projects aim to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency.The PM will also lay the foundation stone for a Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL).The project, estimated to cost around Rs 1,620 crore, will have a capacity of 270 thousand metric tonnes per annum. It aims to manufacture Group II/III lube oil base stocks for producing premium-quality lubricants in India.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas on Sunday got into a heated argument with Delhi Police personnel as they attempted to detain him amid a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas on Sunday got into a heated argument with Delhi Police personnel as they attempted to detain him amid a political row over the detention of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) chief Abhijeet Dipke and other party leaders.Brittas, along with CPM MP A A Rahim, had criticised the police action against Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were reportedly detained aboard their flight from Mumbai after it landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday.Speaking to reporters in Delhi, Brittas said the CJP leaders had been treated worse than hijackers or people accused of major financial scams.“The central government is doing all this because they are scared. The police could have arrested them once they come out of the airport. They could not have escaped from inside the airport. There was no need to detain them from inside the plane,” he said.Brittas also condemned the action against journalists, alleging that several were detained or prevented from reporting on the protests, PTI reported.He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of taking such measures to protect Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Rahim alleged that several CJP activists and protesters who resisted restrictions on the demonstration at Jantar Mantar or objected to the removal of their phones were “brutally tortured”.Dipke, Ranka and Das were released on Sunday after being produced before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court at Delhi Cantonment Police Station.Delhi Police said the three were preventively arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) on October 10 and produced before the court on October 11.The police said the three were released after furnishing a surety bond of Rs 50,000, with a condition to maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh also confirmed their release, saying it was subject to an undertaking to maintain public order. “Condition - no breach of peace for one year,” she posted on X.Before his release, Dipke had alleged in a video posted on Instagram that Delhi Police personnel entered his flight to detain him and his associates after they landed in Delhi.“So, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane. The entire Delhi Police is getting on the plane. This is the fear of Narendra Modi...Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals,” Dipke said.The detention of the CJP leaders came amid a major security clampdown in Delhi on Saturday. Delhi Police detained protesters, activists and political leaders at multiple locations, including along routes leading to Jantar Mantar, where the CJP had planned to hold a demonstration.The party and opposition groups have been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had denied permission for the gathering, and many protesters were detained before they could reach the proposed venue.More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, according to the details provided. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das held a press briefing in New Delhi, hours after being released by a Delhi
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das held a press briefing in New Delhi, hours after being released by a Delhi executive magistrate court on a Rs 50,000 bail bond.During the presser, the duo accused the government of "pushing the country towards civil war".Saurav Das also charged the government with "cloning and hacking" their phone, expressing doubts that the cops would have planted evidence that could later be used against the outfit. He said their phone was snatched without providing them with the seizure memo.Das accused the government of creating an emergency-like situation in the country, similar to the one last seen in 1975.Meanwhile, Abhijeet Dipke, after being released, left for Maharashtra to be with his family as his grandmother passed away on Saturday.Here's what the CJP leaders said: Delhi Police forcefully entered airplane and kidnapped us, Sourav Das said.Delhi Police did not give us formal detention notice; our phones were seized, weren't allowed to contact lawyer, said Saurav Das.We suspect our phones were hacked or cloned. Just as has happened to other activists over the years, we fear they may have hacked into our devices to plant documents or other material to be presented later as evidence... We want to state here that our phones have likely been compromised, Das said.Atmosphere of fear has been created in country. It's clearly being done to save one person, Das said targeting poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar.They said no breach of peace for a year; breach of peace done by PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar: Saurav Das, who was relased after signing a bail condition, said.We want to ask Modi and Shah, why are you trying to save Gyanesh Kumar, Das said."Abhijeet’s grandmother passed away yesterday, and the way Delhi Police conducted themselves upon breaking the news was utterly inhuman. It is shameful to see the police force in the nation's capital behave with such insensitivity," Ashutosh Ranka said."Even at the exact moment Dipke was being told of her demise, police personnel stood around with cameras and microphones, attempting to turn a moment of personal grief into a spectacle," Ranka alleged.A Delhi executive magistrate court on Sunday ordered the release of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, on the condition that they do not engage in any "breach of peace for one year", the party's head of legal affairs, Ratna Singh, said.Delhi Police said a bail bond-cum-surety bond of Rs 50,000 was furnished to ensure "maintaining peace and good behaviour" for a period of one year.Police detained the three leaders from their flight shortly after they landed in the national capital on Saturday, as they planned to protest against Gyanesh Kumar.Delhi Police said it had registered more than 20 FIRs over attempts to forcibly hold a protest on October 10.The cases include charges related to disturbing law and order, obstructing government work and assaulting police personnel. Four people have been detained in connection with the cases, police said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Delhi protest crackdown: 20 FIRs registered, assault on cops among charges
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered 20 FIRs in connection with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered 20 FIRs in connection with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, officials told news agency PTI on Sunday.The cases include charges of assaulting police personnel and obstructing public servants from discharging their duties. One FIR registered at Kamla Market police station relates to the alleged assault on students and manhandling of women during the protest. Four men claiming links to the right-wing Hindu Raksha Dal have been arrested in the case, officials said.The protest, which called for Kumar's resignation, was met with a massive security deployment and widespread detentions across the national capital on Saturday. More than 7,000 people, including opposition leaders and activists, were detained as police erected barricades and deployed thousands of personnel to prevent demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar. Several incidents of stone-throwing were reported, leaving more than 15 police personnel injured, including Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal.Supreme Court steps in over restrictionsAmid the fallout, the Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that Delhi Metro services operate normally, subject to law and order conditions. The bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed that internet services remain undisturbed and that lawyers and journalists not be obstructed from performing their professional duties.The court issued a notice to the Centre while hearing a plea seeking contempt proceedings over alleged violations of its directions concerning restrictions on metro and train services during the protest. It also ordered authorities to remove a notice board outside the Supreme Court premises announcing the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies of five or more people.CJP alleges 'open Emergency'Meanwhile, CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka accused the administration of imposing excessive restrictions to suppress what they described as a youth-led movement."The situation across the country right now mirrors an open Emergency. Such repressive conditions have not been witnessed since the dictatorial regime of 1975," Das said, alleging that Delhi had been turned into a "cantonment".He also criticised the closure of metro stations, suspension of train services and shutdown of markets, claiming the restrictions were inconveniencing ordinary citizens and turning public sentiment against the protest.Ranka separately condemned the police's handling of activist Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that personnel showed insensitivity while informing him of his grandmother's death.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Cillian Murphy bought a century-old Irish cinema he visited as a child; his plan could turn it into a community film venue
articles.summary: Cillian Murphy and his wife, artist Yvonne McGuinness, bought the historic Phoenix Cinema in Dingle, County Kerry, in 2024, hoping to bring the
articles.body: Cillian Murphy and his wife, artist Yvonne McGuinness, bought the historic Phoenix Cinema in Dingle, County Kerry, in 2024, hoping to bring the long-standing venue back to life. The cinema holds a personal connection for the Oscar-winning actor, who visited it during childhood holidays and later watched films there with his own children. After years of closure, the building could once again serve local audiences, with plans to restore its place in the town’s cultural life. The project also reflects the wider challenge of keeping traditional cinemas open.How Cillian Murphy’s childhood cinema became a restoration projectThe Phoenix Cinema has been part of Dingle’s history for more than a century. According to The Independent, the venue opened in 1919 and was built by brothers Jimmy and Johnny Houlihan. Over the years, it served not only as a cinema but also as a dance hall and a venue for concerts and other events.For Murphy, the building was more than an old picture house. In comments reported by The Independent and Sky News in November 2024, he explained that he had watched films there during summer holidays as a young boy. His father had also attended screenings at the cinema when he was younger, creating a connection between generations of the family.Murphy and McGuinness later brought their own children to watch films there. That history helped shape their decision to buy the property after it had been on the market for three years. The couple announced their intention to refurbish the building and reopen its doors, with McGuinness describing a desire to expand its creative possibilities and restore its place in Dingle’s cultural life.Importance of the Phoenix Cinema to DingleThe cinema’s history includes repeated damage and rebuilding. Cinema Treasures, an archive documenting movie theatres, records that the original building was destroyed by fire in 1921 and rebuilt. A second fire damaged the venue in 1938, leading to another reconstruction. The rebuilding helped shape the cinema that became a familiar feature of Dingle.The Independent reports that the venue gained its distinctive art deco facade, phoenix floor mosaic and name during its history. Its location in the town centre also made it an accessible gathering place for residents and visitors.The Phoenix was used for several kinds of entertainment. As well as screening films, it hosted concerts, dances and the Dingle International Film Festival. The Independent also notes that it showed independent and foreign-language films and held a regular Tuesday night film club.Its closure left a gap beyond the loss of a place to watch films. Sky News reported in November 2024 that the Phoenix was the only cinema serving the Dingle Peninsula, with the nearest alternative for local residents in Tralee, almost 30 miles away.The cinema closed during the Covid-19 pandemic. According to Sky News, its previous owners faced rising costs, falling attendance and difficult conditions for screening films. The doors finally shut in November 2021, ending a long period of operation.What will the Phoenix become after redevelopmentThe plans for the building have since moved beyond restoring a traditional cinema. In August 2026, The Journal reported that An Coimisiun Pleanala had granted planning permission for the redevelopment, following an earlier approval from Kerry County Council and appeals by local residents.The approved project will retain the cinema while expanding the site into a wider arts and cultural centre. According to The Journal, the proposed facilities include a multidisciplinary performance space, exhibition and rehearsal areas, artist studios, a cafe, a bar, a restaurant and a redesigned courtyard.The Phoenix’s official website announced the planning approval on 4 August 2026. Murphy, McGuinness and the project team described the centre as a place where the community could gather, create and celebrate the area’s culture and heritage.The website also confirmed that the team had submitted an application to the Rural Regeneration Development Fund, with Kerry County Council acting as its lead partner. The application represents a further step towards the next phase of development, although planning permission alone does not mean the renovation has been completed.The restored cinema could serve the wider communityThe project arrives at a time when independent cinemas face pressure from changing viewing habits, streaming services and operating costs.The Irish Times reported that appeals had been lodged against the Phoenix redevelopment plans, with a decision then pending. The Journal’s August report subsequently confirmed that planning permission had been granted despite objections concerning the development’s scale, parking, access and proposed mix of uses.The restored Phoenix could offer Dingle more than a return to its former screening schedule. Its combination of cinema, performance and exhibition spaces is intended to provide a home for different forms of local creativity and give artists opportunities to work and present their projects.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 1958, Texas voters rejected a $15 million reservoir plan; 68 years later, a judge overturned a new permit for Lake Ringgold after ranchers warned the project could flood more than 16,000 acres of farmland
articles.summary: A reservoir plan rejected by voters in the water district serving Wichita Falls in 1958 is facing another major setback nearly seven decades later.
articles.body: A reservoir plan rejected by voters in the water district serving Wichita Falls in 1958 is facing another major setback nearly seven decades later. On October 9, 2026, a judge overturned the state permit for Lake Ringgold, a proposed reservoir that could flood more than 16,000 acres of agricultural land and wildlife habitat in Clay County, Texas. The project was proposed by the city of Wichita Falls to help secure water supplies for North Texas during future droughts. But ranchers and conservation groups challenged the plan, arguing that it would damage productive grazing land, affect wildlife and force families to give up properties they had owned for generations.As reported by American media portal News Channel 6, Travis County District Judge Maya Guerra Gamble overturned the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality’s decision to issue the permit after hearing arguments in Austin. The ruling is a major victory for landowners who have opposed the project, although the city has said it may appeal. The dispute centres on two competing concerns: how Wichita Falls can secure a reliable water supply for the future, and whether the proposed reservoir is justified given the amount of land and habitat it would affect.A reservoir plan that dates back to 1958The Lake Ringgold proposal has a history stretching back to the 1950s. Historical reporting records that voters in the water district serving Wichita Falls rejected the Ringgold project in 1958, when its estimated cost was $15 million. This was not a statewide Texas referendum. The idea returned to the forefront after a severe drought affected North Texas between 2010 and 2015. According to The Texas Tribune, the drought came close to draining Wichita Falls’ two main reservoirs, Lake Arrowhead and Lake Kickapoo. The city imposed strict water-use restrictions and explored ways to reduce demand. Russell Schreiber, the city’s public works director, described the situation as “very devastating” in an interview with The Texas Tribune, recalling how the reservoirs approached critically low levels.From July 2014 to July 2015, Wichita Falls also used direct potable reuse, a process that treats wastewater so it can be used as drinking water. The initiative helped reduce demand on the two reservoirs by 75%, but their combined storage still fell to about 20% of capacity. The experience pushed city officials to revisit the reservoir proposal. The city argues that another reservoir would provide an additional source of water during future droughts and help protect the region from shortages.What the proposed Lake Ringgold would involveThe reservoir would be created by building a dam on the Little Wichita River, about half a mile upstream from where it joins the Red River. The site is in Clay County, approximately 30 miles east of Wichita Falls. According to The Texas Tribune, the project was estimated to cost $443 million and could provide a yield of 65,000 acre-feet of water per year. One acre-foot is the volume of water needed to cover one acre of land to a depth of one foot.The city would need about 24,000 acres for the overall project, including the reservoir, pumping facilities and a transmission line to carry water to treatment facilities in Wichita Falls. It owned approximately 6,662 acres of the required land, meaning additional property would need to be acquired through purchases or eminent domain. Opponents of the project said more than 25 ranching families could be forced to sell all or part of their land if the reservoir went ahead. The proposed lake itself would cover more than 16,000 acres, including productive agricultural land and wildlife habitat. The Texas & Southwestern Cattle Raisers Association (TSCRA) said the reservoir would displace ranching operations and permanently alter the landscape.Ranchers fear losing land held by their families for generationsFor ranchers in Clay County, the concern is not only about the acreage that would be submerged. The land is also where they raise livestock, maintain their livelihoods and have built family homes. According to a May 2024 report by The Texas Tribune, ranchers described how the reservoir could cut through grazing land, flood ancestral properties and submerge homes where their children had grown up.Why the permit went to courtThe Texas Commission on Environmental Quality approved the city's permit for Lake Ringgold on June 27, 2024. The decision came despite opposition from landowners and conservation groups, including the Texas Conservation Alliance. The dispute followed a contested-case hearing in which opponents questioned whether the reservoir was necessary at the proposed scale and argued that its environmental and agricultural costs had not been adequately justified.According to The Texas Tribune, an administrative judge had previously recommended denying the permit, citing concerns about whether the project’s scale was justified by the city's projected water needs. The city, however, maintained that it needed to plan for future population growth and drought. The landowners' challenge eventually reached Travis County District Court. On October 9, 2026, Judge Maya Guerra Gamble overturned the state agency's decision to issue the permit. The ruling overturned the permit decision; it did not establish that the region no longer needs additional water supplies.What happens to Lake Ringgold now?The ruling has overturned the state permit, but the city's plans may not be over. Wichita Falls Mayor Tim Short told News Channel 6 that the city had 30 days to appeal and would discuss its next steps with legal counsel. The report did not say that an appeal had already been filed. The city also reiterated its commitment to securing long-term water supplies for Wichita Falls and the surrounding region. The TSCRA, which supported affected landowners during the proceedings, described the ruling as an important milestone.The judge's decision does not remove the region's need to plan for future droughts, but it has halted the project under the permit that was challenged. Any further steps will depend on the city's response and the next stage of the legal process. The Lake Ringgold proposal has been debated for decades, from the $15 million plan rejected by voters in the Wichita Falls water district in 1958 to the $443 million project considered in recent years. Its future now depends on whether the city can overcome the latest legal setback while addressing the concerns of ranchers who fear losing their land and livelihoods.You use AI every day. articles.body: The Houthis on Sunday renewed their warning against the use of Saudi airspace by airlines, companies and travellers with the exception of Mecca and Medina airports.The warning has been issued to all shipping companies, airlines, experts, employees, workers, and travellers, Houthi spokesperson Yahya Saree said on X."They are exposed to targeting and a theater for operations by our forces", Yahya said."With the exception of the airports of Mecca Al-Mukarramah and Medina Al-Munawwarah", he added.The cities of Mecca and Medina are among the holiest sites in Islam and owe immense religious significance to both Sunni and Shia sects.Houthi remarks come a day after they targeted Saudi's Riyadh's international airport, reportedly killing 12 people and wounding over 300 others.Yahya described the targeting of Saudi airports as a tit-for-tat action.According to Saudi Gazette, citing the General Authority of Civil Aviation, the fatalities included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals and one national each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan."The Armed Forces affirm that they are steadfast in establishing the announced equations: airport for airport, siege for siege, and escalation for escalation, until achieving their objectives," Yahya said.Saudi vows retaliation as Trump hints entryThe Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen has vowed a firm response to the attack, describing it as a war crime. According to Saudi Gazette, coalition spokesperson major general Turki Al-Maliki said the October 10 strike targeted a passenger terminal, resulting in civilian casualties.Al-Maliki blamed Yemen’s Houthi militia for the attack, calling it a violation of international humanitarian law and customary rules of war. He said the coalition’s Joint Forces Command would respond firmly in accordance with international humanitarian law.Riyadh has intensified its military involvement in Yemen in recent weeks, carrying out strikes against the Houthis and supporting a counter-offensive by the Yemeni government after the group seized strategic territory along the Red Sea coast last month.When asked about the Saturday attack, US President Donald Trump said America could join Saudi Arabia’s military strikes against the Houthis, adding that his administration was reviewing the latest developments and could decide on the matter soon.“We may. We're going to look at it soon. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly”, Trump said.“We're going to take a look”, he added.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2015, Google helped 'release' 3 million mosquitoes in Australia; the theory was simple ...
articles.summary: A Google-backed mosquito control project in Australia successfully released around three million specially bred male mosquitoes and reduced populations of
articles.body: A Google-backed mosquito control project in Australia successfully released around three million specially bred male mosquitoes and reduced populations of an invasive disease-carrying species by as much as 95%, according to a report by The Conversation. The findings are drawing renewed attention as Alphabet's Debug initiative seeks approval to release up to 32 million sterilised male mosquitoes in California and Florida to combat mosquito-borne diseases.Nigel Beebe, a professor at the University of Queensland, wrote in The Conversation that the trial showed releasing specially bred male mosquitoes can dramatically suppress populations of Aedes aegypti, an invasive species that spreads dengue, Zika, chikungunya and yellow fever.How the Australian trial of Google's life sciences division workedThe work began in 2015, when Beebe's team traveled to Silicon Valley to meet scientists at Verily, Google's life sciences division. Their goals matched a government-funded Australian research project on environmentally friendly ways to suppress invasive mosquitoes.The method relies on Wolbachia, a bacterium found naturally in many insects. Certain strains make mating incompatible, so the eggs do not develop. Because female Aedes aegypti generally mate only once, a single incompatible mating leaves them with no viable offspring. Beebe said the theory is that releasing enough Wolbachia-carrying males will make the population decline over time, and that the males' large, bushy antennae help them find the last remaining females.Far north Queensland's Cassowary Coast offered favorable conditions. Its towns have abundant Aedes aegypti, while surrounding farmland limits movement between communities. Before any release, the team spent two years on field surveys and community engagement, meeting households, community groups, First Nations leaders and councils. The project, called "Debug Innisfail," then received approval from multiple regulators.During a 20-week release in 2018, about three million Wolbachia-carrying males were released into three towns, while control towns were monitored without releases. Verily built custom technology, including machine-learning-based systems to separate males from females so that only males were released.Verily contributed specialised engineering tools, including machine learning systems capable of separating male and female mosquitoes, ensuring only non-biting males were released.The results were significant. According to findings published in 2021, mosquito populations started declining within four weeks of the releases. In two towns, suppression effects persisted into the following year. One location recorded only a handful of Aedes aegypti mosquitoes 12 months later, representing roughly 95% population suppression.Results of Google’s mosquito trialMosquito populations in the release towns began falling within four weeks, compared with the control towns. The findings were published in 2021. In two towns, the suppression lasted into the following year. In one, monitoring found only a handful of Aedes aegypti 12 months later, which Beebe said corresponds to roughly 95% suppression.Beebe's takeaways for the USBeebe argued the Australian experience speaks to several American worries:* Ecology: The ecological impact is likely to be very small. Aedes aegypti is invasive in Australia and elsewhere, lives exclusively around people and bites mainly humans, so removing it from cities has few ecological consequences.* Scale: The approach can work across whole towns. Adult mosquitoes live only days, but continuous releases of highly competitive males can substantially reduce populations.* Durability: Benefits can carry over into later seasons after releases stop.He cautioned that success depends on local ecology, mosquito movement patterns and community participation, and said the technology alone is not enough. He also said researchers are still working toward better ways to separate male mosquitoes mechanically, which would be more useful in developing countries.What the US is consideringGoogle's Debug initiative, now part of Alphabet, has asked the federal government for permission to release up to 32 million sterilized male mosquitoes in California and Florida. Beebe said the plan involves releasing more than 16 million insects a year for two years.Male mosquitoes do not bite or carry disease. The hope is that they will mate with disease-carrying females, whose eggs then fail to hatch, and that mosquito numbers will fall. Beebe said the American public has questions about whether the releases are safe, whether they will work at scale and what happens afterward.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Competition of anarchy’: BJP hits out at Rahul Gandhi, Arvind Kejriwal amid CEC protest row
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Bansuri Swaraj on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MP Bansuri Swaraj on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal of engaging in a “competition of anarchy”, alleging that voters had rejected both parties and that their leaders were making excuses for their electoral defeats.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, the New Delhi MP said the Congress and AAP had failed to win the people's trust and were looking for reasons to explain their setbacks instead of engaging in constructive politics.“It appears a competition of anarchy is emerging between Arvind Kejriwal and Rahul Gandhi—whether it is the Aam Aadmi Party or the Congress party, the voters of this nation have rejected both. Having failed to secure power through the popular mandate, they are now seeking excuses for their defeat,” Swaraj said.Her remarks came amid a political confrontation over the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, which saw heavy police deployment and the detention of several Opposition leaders in Delhi.Rahul Gandhi announces fresh INDIA bloc protestLeader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has announced that the Congress and the INDIA bloc will return to the streets on October 12, alleging that Delhi Police personnel and BJP workers used violence against students and women during the protests.In a series of posts on X on Saturday, the Raebareli MP accused the government of attempting to suppress the voices of young people and students. He also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi by referring to the fictional villain Mogambo from the film Mr India.The Congress leader accused Union home minister Amit Shah's Delhi Police of resorting to “thuggery” and alleged that workers of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and BJP had been allowed to attack women and young protesters.“Amit Shah's Delhi Police has not only resorted to thuggery itself but is also giving a free hand and encouragement to the real goons of the RSS-BJP to perpetrate violence against women and the youth,” he said.He added that attempts to suppress young people would only intensify their anger.“As I had said, the more 'Mogambo Modi' and his government try to suppress them, the more the anger of Gen Z and the students will intensify,” Rahul said.Announcing the next protest, he said, “On Monday, October 12, the Congress, the entire INDIA alliance, and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers. And this time, too, the voice will resonate across the nation-louder than ever before.”Rahul also said the opposition would meet the Chief Justice on Monday to seek accountability over the alleged violence and the treatment of protesters.Kejriwal attacks PM Modi, faces gurdwara complaintAAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal also targeted PM Modi over the police crackdown on the CJP-led protest, invoking Hitler to criticise the treatment of demonstrators.In a video posted on X, Kejriwal alleged that young women, lawyers and journalists were mistreated during Saturday's operation and warned that the demand for resignation could extend beyond CEC Gyanesh Kumar.“The way Modi ji unleashed a reign of terror yesterday, he crossed all limits and left even Hitler behind,” Kejriwal said, adding, “It should not come to a point where, along with Gyanesh Kumar, Modi ji himself is forced to resign this time”.Separately, the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC) approached the Delhi Police with a complaint against Kejriwal and other AAP leaders, accusing them of disrupting the sanctity of Gurudwara Bangla Sahib during the protests and circulating misleading videos of the incident.The committee alleged that protesters raised political slogans inside the premises and sought action against those involved. Kejriwal and AAP leaders have maintained that protesters took shelter inside the gurdwara after police stopped them from proceeding towards Jantar Mantar.#WATCH | Delhi: Harmeet Singh Kalka, President, Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee (DSGMC), says, "There is great resentment within the Sikh community regarding the manner in which some AAP workers entered Gurudwara Bangla Sahib posing as protesters, unfurled banners and posters, and staged a demonstration. We have taken strict action against them and have also lodged a police complaint against their party supremo, Arvind Kejriwal... Some police personnel also went there; we condemn that, and today we have instructed the DCP to direct police personnel to avoid entering the 'Guru Ghar' in uniform. Even though it is a public thoroughfare and they did not actually step onto the Gurudwara premises itself, police personnel should exercise restraint given the current atmosphere. All the protesters were sent by Arvind Kejriwal, and this is a matter for investigation because the workers we have identified are all associated with the AAP. Furthermore, as soon as this action took place, AAP MLAs, their workers, and even Bhagwant Mann himself tweeted about the police presence inside the 'Guru Ghar', misleading people with incomplete information. People were told that the police had entered the 'Guru Ghar', whereas not a single police officer even stepped onto the Gurudwara's steps. If anyone comes there to stage a protest—whether it is Arvind Kejriwal, Rahul Gandhi, or even the National President of the BJP—we will not allow anyone to demonstrate inside the Gurudwara." He further says, "I would say the same thing to every agitator exercising their right to protest... We saw thousands—in fact, I believe lakhs of 'Sangat' arrive over a span of three days; no one was stopped then, nor will anyone be stopped now or in the future. We have no issue with protesters coming here. However, we will not allow protests to take place inside the 'Guru Ghar'. As you all saw in the videos, they brought banners and posters and started raising slogans—actions that run contrary to the sanctity of the 'Guru Ghar'."— ANI (@ANI) October 11, 2026The police, however, said personnel used a common passage to reach the protesters and did not enter the main sanctum.BJP targets Congress over JNU professor's dismissalSeparately, Swaraj launched another attack on Rahul and the Congress over the dismissal of party MP and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam following an inquiry into sexual harassment allegations.Swaraj questioned why the Congress had not initiated disciplinary action against Akoijam, asking whether “nari samman” was merely a slogan for the party rather than a policy.“Rahul Gandhi, this nation calls you out for your selective outrage, your motivated stance and for your false narrative,” she said.“If 'smash the patriarchy' is not a motivated stance and not mere political rhetoric for you, then take action against your MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam,” she added.JNU dismissed Akoijam from service with immediate effect on Friday after its inquiry found him guilty, PTI reported. He was a professor at the university's Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.At least 11 female students filed sexual harassment complaints against him in May. The complainants alleged that he invited students to his campus residence under the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to sexually harass them. articles.title: Arunachal cabinet approves key reforms in technical education & healthcare
articles.summary: Arunachal cabinet okays AICTE-based recruitment rules for technical colleges, Women Helpline 181 posts, new food safety officers, and leprosy staff pay hike.
articles.body: Itanagar: The Arunachal Pradesh Cabinet, chaired by chief minister Pema Khandu, on Sunday approved a series of measures to strengthen technical education, improve healthcare delivery, enhance women’s safety and streamline institutional administration across the state.The Cabinet approved uniform recruitment rules for 12 categories of teaching and technical posts in govt engineering and polytechnic colleges in line with the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) Regulations, 2019.The rules will apply to posts including principals, professors, associate professors, assistant professors, workshop superintendents, assistant librarians, laboratory assistants, senior technical assistants, system analysts and heads of departments.The move is aimed at ensuring greater transparency, uniformity and merit-based recruitment in technical education institutions.To strengthen support services for women, the Cabinet sanctioned 20 posts for implementing the Women Helpline-181 scheme under Mission Shakti. The 24-hour toll-free helpline will provide assistance to women in distress and connect them with medical care, shelter, legal aid, counselling and emotional support.The Cabinet also approved the creation of five Food Safety Officer posts under the Group B, Gazetted Non-Ministerial category to address staff shortages and strengthen food-safety monitoring and enforcement.In another healthcare-related decision, it approved an increase in grade pay for various categories of employees working under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme. The measure is intended to ensure wage parity, improve staff morale and strengthen patient care and rehabilitation services.The Cabinet also approved the renaming of three educational institutions in honour of prominent personalities. articles.title: MacKenzie Scott gave Maliasili $15 million after an earlier grant helped create a conservation fund; that fund has since backed 28 organisations
articles.summary: A $15 million unrestricted gift from MacKenzie Scott is giving Maliasili a new source of capital as the African conservation organisation begins work
articles.body: A $15 million unrestricted gift from MacKenzie Scott is giving Maliasili a new source of capital as the African conservation organisation begins work under a new 2030 strategic plan. The grant, received in late 2025, is the second time Scott has supported Maliasili. Her earlier funding, awarded in 2021, helped establish the Maliasili Conservation Fund, a pooled funding model designed to give conservation organisations more flexible and longer-term financial support. As reported by Maliasili, since then, that fund has attracted more than $14 million and supported 28 partner organisations over three years. Maliasili says those partners have also used the funding to bring in additional resources, strengthening the model beyond the original grants.How Scott’s $15 million grant could change conservation funding for MaliasiliThe latest $15 million award arrived as Maliasili was preparing to begin a new phase of its work. The organisation describes the money as one-time unrestricted funding, giving it considerable scope in how the grant can be used within its wider strategy.For Maliasili, the timing matters because the organisation is beginning its new strategic plan for 2030. Rather than treating Scott's latest contribution as a standalone grant, it plans to use part of the funding to expand an approach that emerged from her first gift.Scott's support has become associated with unrestricted or trust-based philanthropy, in which organisations are given greater discretion over how money is allocated. In Maliasili's case, the earlier grant was used to test a funding structure intended to address a longstanding issue for conservation groups: access to reliable core funding rather than money tied only to individual projects.The conservation fund that grew from Scott’s first grantMaliasili used its 2021 funding from Scott as seed capital for the Maliasili Conservation Fund, known as MCF. Instead of operating as a conventional grant programme, the fund combines flexible financial support with organisational strengthening and help with fundraising.That distinction has shaped how the fund has developed. Partner organisations receive core and multi-year funding, while also getting support intended to improve their ability to operate, raise money and build stronger institutions.Over the following three years, MCF secured more than $14 million in additional funding. Maliasili says the fund supported 28 partners during that period. The organisation also points to the money that those grants helped generate beyond the initial investment. For every $1 provided through the conservation fund, partners unlocked roughly another $3 in funding, according to Maliasili.Why flexible funding is at the centre of the modelMany conservation organisations operate with restricted project grants, where funding is attached to a particular activity or outcome. That can leave less room for spending on staff, organisational development, planning or other needs that do not fit neatly into a project budget.MCF was designed differently. Its funding could be used more flexibly, alongside practical support intended to strengthen the organisations receiving it. Maliasili says this combination has helped its partners become stronger organisations while increasing their capacity to deliver conservation work. The organisation is now seeking to extend that approach to more groups and across a broader geographical area.Maliasili builds on its $14 million conservation funding experimentThe $15 million grant will provide seed capital for the new pooled funding mechanism. Maliasili plans to make this a significant part of its strategy through 2030, building on what it says has already worked through MCF.The organisation sees flexible funding as a way of drawing more resources towards African conservation groups working directly with communities and landscapes. Those organisations often have long-term conservation responsibilities but can face difficulty accessing funding on terms that allow them to invest in their own priorities.Maliasili's new approach is intended to address that gap without treating the initial grant as the end of the funding process. The organisation describes the capital as a catalyst, with the expectation that it can help bring further resources into locally led conservation work.The experience of MCF provides the basis for that expectation. More than $14 million has flowed into the fund since its creation, while its 28 partners have collectively used the support to strengthen their organisations and attract further funding.A wider role for African conservation organisationsThe expansion also reflects a broader shift in how Maliasili wants resources to reach conservation groups. Its stated focus is on African organisations that are closely connected to the communities and landscapes where conservation work takes place.Under the new fund, Maliasili intends to reach a wider set of partners rather than concentrating the approach on the organisations already supported through MCF.The structure will continue to emphasise flexible capital, organisational support and fundraising capacity. Partner involvement in designing the fund is also expected to remain part of the model.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Army is the rule, army is the law': India tears into Pakistan at UN over minority rights
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India on Sunday accused Pakistan of using allegations about the treatment of religious minorities in India to divert attention from its own
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India on Sunday accused Pakistan of using allegations about the treatment of religious minorities in India to divert attention from its own record on minority rights, judicial independence and press freedom.Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly's Sixth Committee during discussions on the rule of law at national and international levels, Mythili R, a counsellor at India's Permanent Mission to the UN, accused Islamabad of preaching legal accountability abroad while undermining it at home.She described Pakistan as a country where "the army is the rule and the law", alleging that judicial independence had been weakened, civilians were being tried in military courts and political opposition was being suppressed."At the UN, Pakistan lectures others on the rule of law. Yet at home, the Army is the rule, and the Army is the law. Judicial independence undermined, civilians tried in military courts, political opposition suppressed," she said, according to a statement shared by India's Permanent Mission to the UN on X.India slams Pakistan's record on minorities Mythili also challenged Pakistan's claims on minority rights, pointing to what she described as a steady decline in the proportion of minorities in the country's population since its creation.She questioned press freedom in Pakistan, referring to the Foreign Media Facilitation Guidelines issued by its Ministry of Information and Broadcasting. Under the guidelines, foreign media outlets must obtain a "No-Objection Certificate" to report freely outside Islamabad, Lahore and Karachi.The Indian diplomat accused Pakistan of repeatedly failing to uphold the rule of law and said its focus on India was misplaced."The rule of law bestows an obligation upon those in positions of power to do good for those they govern. However, in the case of Pakistan, unfortunately, this promise is broken again and again. It is not India that has an obsession with Pakistan but the other way round," she said.India defends Operation SindoorThe exchange also brought the two countries' sharply contrasting positions on cross-border terrorism into focus. Mythili defended India's response to the Pakistan-backed terror attack in Pahalgam last year, which killed 26 people, describing Operation Sindoor as measured and proportionate.She urged Pakistan to stop repeating what she called baseless allegations against India, arguing that doing so would not shield its representatives from accountability for promises made to their own people."Reading and re-reading the same laundry list of false allegations against my country will not absolve Pakistani representatives of the promises that they have made to their people and which they have no intention to keep," she said.Taking a swipe at Pakistan's claims about the outcome of the military confrontation, she added, "As far as the result of the same is concerned, if bombed airfields and destroyed hangars are victory, they are welcome to enjoy it," she said.India warns against nuclear blackmailThe latest exchange followed India's response on Saturday to Pakistan's remarks at the UN General Assembly's First Committee, where discussions included disarmament and international security.First Secretary Anmol Sher Singh Bedi said India's military posture was defensive and guided by its own security requirements, rather than directed against any particular country. He defended India's response to the Pahalgam attack as "measured, targeted, and non-escalatory" and an exercise of its right to self-defence.Bedi laid out India's position on terrorism and the risk of nuclear escalation, stating, "First: Any terrorist attack against India will receive a fitting response; Second: India will not bow to nuclear blackmail; Third: India will make no distinction between those who sponsor terrorism and those who mastermind it."He argued that states could not escape responsibility for supporting militant groups by acting through non-state actors, adding that such actions did not diminish India's right to defend itself."Escalation concerns are best judged by conduct, over rhetoric. Nuclear weapons must not be a routine instrument of statecraft. Relying on a nuclear overhang to limit the consequences of sub-conventional activity raises escalation risk, not restraint," he said.Bedi also criticised what he described as a recurring pattern in regional crises, involving provocation, denial of responsibility and calls for restraint after retaliation.He said, "where those in power are neither elected by nor accountable to the people, crisis becomes an instrument of power and instability becomes useful."Reaffirming India's stated commitment to peace, Bedi said the country did not seek conflict but would respond to threats. He concluded, "without accountability for reckless actions, peace merely becomes a pause between crises."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
